eligibility_reason: Self-replication ('A Replication Study') of Yasuda et al. (2025): the original identified an EVCI subgroup using cognitive data from the Osaka cohort only; this paper gathers new cognitive data for EV individuals from the other COCORO cohorts (27 individuals, 8 cohorts) and tests whether the EVCI subgroup and its characteristics reappear.

effects.original_title: Proposal for a Novel Classification of Patients With Enlarged Ventricles and Cognitive Impairment Based on Data-Driven Analysis of Neuroimaging Results in Patients With Psychiatric Disorders
effects.original_authors: Yasuda, Yuka; Ito, Satsuki; Matsumoto, Junya
effects.outcome: Existence of a subgroup with enlarged ventricles and moderate/severe cognitive impairment (EVCI; >=20-point drop from JART premorbid IQ to WAIS current IQ) among individuals with enlarged ventricles, and its predominant association with schizophrenia
effects.contrast: EVCI vs EV-non-CI individuals among those with enlarged lateral ventricles (average z > 3)
effects.description: Among individuals with enlarged lateral ventricles, a distinct subgroup (~27%) shows marked cognitive impairment (EVCI), and this subgroup consists predominantly of patients with schizophrenia (8 of 9).
effects.citation_sentence: In our previous study [6], we performed data‐driven classification based on large‐scale neuroimaging datasets to identify a novel subtype of psychiatric disorders characterized by pronounced EV and CI (i.e., EVCI). ... Yasuda et al. [6] performed a large‐scale data‐driven analysis and found that patients with EVCI constitute a distinct subgroup characterized by a high prevalence of schizophrenia.
effects.evidence: Results/Table 1: 'A total of 18.5% (n = 5) were classified as having EVCI'; 'all individuals classified as having EVCI had a diagnosis of schizophrenia'. Conclusions: 'The present study validated the existence of the EVCI subgroup in independent cohorts. EVCI may be more frequently observed among males and is predominantly associated with a diagnosis of schizophrenia.' Abstract: 'This study validated the existence of the EVCI subgroup in independent cohorts, thus supporting our previous findings.'
effects.notes: Original DOI taken from the reference's pub-id in the source XML (ref 6: e70010, doi 10.1002/npr2.70010, PMID 40011069); the rendered references list no DOI. Only the first three original authors are given ('et al.'). Result: authors explicitly say 'validated' and 'provided additional support for our previous findings'; caveats: EVCI n = 5, cognitive data for only 27/146 EV individuals, no inferential test of the subgroup claim itself (prevalence 18.5% vs original 27.3%; 5/5 vs 8/9 schizophrenia). A stricter coder could call it inconclusive on power grounds, but the codebook says follow the explicit statement. Enumeration: I coded the subgroup + schizophrenia-predominance as one claim, since the paper frames the original finding as one ('a distinct subgroup characterized by a high prevalence of schizophrenia'). Possible additional splits a second coder might make: (a) male predominance in EVCI ('Consistent with our previous study, the present study also revealed a higher prevalence of males in the EVCI group' — 3/5 male, but the EV-non-CI group is 77% male, chi-square p = 0.43, so as a between-group comparison it is not supported); (b) the EVCI vs EV-non-CI comparison pattern (lower current IQ, no difference in premorbid IQ or ventricle z-score; 'consistent with the trends observed in our previous study (see Table S1 ... table 5 in the previous paper)') — the CI/current-IQ difference is true by construction, so I treated these as descriptive characterization rather than separate claims. Replication type: same EV definition (z > 3) and CI criterion, but other cohorts/sites and current IQ also measured with WAIS-IV or the simplified WAIS (the original used WAIS-III + JART) — coded close experiment (equivalent alternative measure); direct is a defensible alternative. Note the EV individuals were identified from the same 186-person MRI pool reported in the original paper; what is new is the cognitive data for the 146 non-Osaka EV individuals.
